data.title: Kospi rises 7%, Nikkei up nearly 5% post Wall Street gains sparked by Nvidia surge
data.description:
Asian shares gained after a wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia Corp fueled a global equities rally and resulted in the Wall Street witnessing its best day ever since April 9, 2025.

The MSCI Inc's Asia Pacific equities increased 1.8%, rebounding post eight straight sessions of losses pushing the gauge close to a bear market. The gains were led by South Korea with its Kospi index rising over 7%. Japan's Nikkei index was up nearly 5% as trading resumed post a long weekend.

The gains come after the S&P 500 snapped a seven-day losing streak, rising 4.7%, while the Nasdaq 100 climbed 6.9%, pulling back from the brink of a bear market and a gauge of semiconductor jumped 14%. Nvidia shares surged 31%, the most since 2003.

Short-term Treasuries were steady and crude oil prices held its losses. Gold extended its gains and was trading around $3,640 an ounce.

The global stock rally marked a dramatic reversal post the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entering corrections on Friday. Huang’s return to Nvidia at the center of the artificial intelligence boom reignited enthusiasm for AI stocks post his exit throwing the trade into turmoil and raising questions over whether future profits can justify the industry’s surge in debt-financed spending.

With inputs from Bloomberg

data.title: Venezuela signs 84 energy deals, reforms power sector
data.description:
Venezuela has signed 84 oil and gas agreements so far this year, acting President Delcy Rodríguez said, El Periódico de la Energía reported. Rodríguez also signed into law an electricity reform that allows private and foreign companies to generate power.

Rodríguez took office after Nicolás Maduro was captured on January 3, and her government reformed the hydrocarbons law that same month. Since then, Caracas has struck deals with Spain's Repsol, US majors Chevron and ExxonMobil, Britain's Shell and Italy's Eni. The most prominent was an August agreement giving Washington access to 25% of Venezuela's oil reserves for at least 25 years.

Opposition groups and oil specialists have criticised what they describe as a lack of transparency in contracts signed with foreign firms.

Rodríguez spoke by video link to the Expo Venezuela Energética Oriente 2026 in Anzoátegui, one of four eastern states that make up the Orinoco oil belt. She said the agreements signed by state oil company PDVSA were meant to secure the country's present.

She repeated that crude output stands at 1.269mn barrels per day, with 730,000 barrels coming from the Orinoco belt. PDVSA President Héctor Obregón recently forecast that production would finish the year at 1.3mn barrels per day.

Parliament passed the new Organic Law on the Electricity System and Service nine days before Rodríguez signed it. Under the law, the state operator, joint ventures and licensed private companies may all generate electricity. Concessions to private firms can run for a maximum of 25 years.

Oil companies must guarantee a continuous and stable power supply for their primary operations through self-generation, cogeneration or contracts with third parties.

Rodríguez said the reform would let domestic and international private investors take part in generation and would improve the national power service. She described it as a historic step forward.

data.title: India boosts Venezuelan crude and US gas imports
data.description:
India has sharply increased its imports of Venezuelan crude oil and American liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), drawing the energy relationship between New Delhi and Washington closer, Nikkei Asia reported.

The rise comes as the two governments continue talks on a trade agreement that has been repeatedly delayed and remains contentious.

The shift in buying follows a dispute that began more than a year ago, when US President Donald Trump confronted India over its purchases of Russian crude. Since then, Indian buyers have turned to Venezuelan oil and US LPG in greater volumes, even though the wider trade negotiations between the two countries have not concluded.

Reliance Industries accounts for most of India's purchases of Venezuelan crude, which are processed at its Jamnagar refinery in the western state of Gujarat.

data.title: Asian Equities Rebound as Huang Reinstatement Sparks AI-Stock Rally
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities rebounded Tuesday morning after Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of Nvidia sparked a rally in artificial-intelligence stocks.

The U.S. chip maker's board on Monday reinstated Huang less than two weeks after pushing him out over issues including extramarital affairs. The decision followed intense pressure from Silicon Valley, Wall Street investors, and the White House.

"Huang reinstated as CEO triggers a tremendous tech-led 'risk-back-on' rally," said Vishnu Varathan, head of Macro Strategy for APAC at Mizuho Securities (Singapore). "Markets cheered the news of what is perceived to be stability returning to the wider AI sector as Nvidia with Jensen at the helm was deemed to be the requisite connective tissue of the industry."

However, the company and its reinstated leader face a series of investigations by entities ranging from the Securities and Exchange Commission to a committee of the board itself.

Asian equities rebounded from Monday's selloff. South Korea's Kospi climbed 7.1%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rising 8.8% and 6.5%, respectively. Kospi futures rose more than 6%, triggering a five-minute trading halt by Korea Exchange.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average advanced 4.8%. Resonac Holdings, a supplier of front-end and back-end semiconductor packaging materials, surged 16.4%, Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic semiconductor test equipment for semiconductor industry, jumped 15.6%, and Murata Manufacturing, a manufacturer of electronic components, added 14.9%.

Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI advanced 1.3% and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index gained 1.3%.

"Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, in an email.

Meanwhile, crude oil futures were mixed as traders parsed ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

The U.S. is investigating Iran's potential involvement in dozens of cyberattacks against energy tankers amid worries that Tehran is widening the war with cyber operations and terror plots against Americans far from the Middle East.

As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials and others familiar with the matter.

"Iran continues to attack vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, with [President] Trump announcing it has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time of over the year," ANZ Research analysts said in a report. "Despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, the oil market remains under severe strain," the analysts added.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures were little changed at $80.16 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures edged 0.1% lower to $89.28 a barrel, ICE data showed.
